Why

A tool for getting heavy CAD assemblies into the browser.

The problem it works on is a practical one. A real-world STEP file can hold 400 identical bolts, 80 duplicate brackets and half a million degenerate triangles, and a browser is still expected to draw it. MeshOptimiser reads the assembly, recognises the parts that are the same and keeps one mesh with a list of positions, re-tessellates the bad geometry, and drops what is too small to see.

What comes out is a compressed GLB and a viewer to look at it in: the assembly tree, recolouring, mesh tools, a library of parts to add, export. It runs locally, with Python and a browser, as an open, self-hosted take on what preprocessors like Pixyz do.

What the pipeline collapses
400 bolts × 50 KB→1 mesh × 50 KB + 400 transforms
80 brackets × 12 KB→1 mesh × 12 KB + 80 transforms
500K bad triangles→Adaptive re-tessellation, size-culled
320 MB STEP→11 MB Meshopt-compressed GLB

How it works

Three steps from STEP to the browser.

  1. 01

    STEP in

    Drop a .step or .stp file on the welcome screen, or run the converter from the command line.

  2. 02

    Convert

    OCCT reads the full assembly tree with names and colours; duplicate parts are instanced, surfaces tessellated adaptively, tiny parts culled, then the result is compressed.

  3. 03

    GLB out

    Open it in the built-in WebGPU viewer: inspect, recolour, reduce, tidy the hierarchy, and export.

In motion

Tools that do one job, and say what it saved.

All features

A closer look

Built for assemblies with thousands of parts.

01

A drawer full of parts

Hex bolts, wing nuts, pillow blocks, I-beams, gears, a stepper motor: 86 parametric parts on six shelves. Drag one out and a see-through copy shows where it will stand, square to the face under the pointer. Let go and it is there.

02

878 parts nobody will ever see

Select hidden parts looks at the model from every side and picks out what cannot be seen from any of them. On this assembly that is more than half the parts and 2.4 million of its 5.4 million triangles, selected in one step and ready to delete.

03

82% lighter, still recognisable

Smart fit used to turn a bracket into a brick. Blocks rebuilds each part from a coarse grid, with its steps, arms and openings where they were. This drive unit went from 16,812 triangles to 3,048 in one command.

04

A bolt that brings its own nut

Tick it on, choose the nut, and set how far from the head it sits. It is part of the bolt’s own shape, in the bolt’s thread: one part in the tree, one undo step, and it cannot run off the end.

Latest release

v0.13.0

Full changelog

It feels like an app. MeshOptimiser installs to the desktop with an icon of its own, opens in a window with no address bar, browser tabs or extension buttons, and can fold its title bar away. The scene tabs grew up with it, and a view that is moving gives up what you cannot see anyway.

  • NewInstall it: Chrome and Edge offer Install, and the app gets a desktop shortcut and a window to itself. start.bat opens that window directly, with nothing of the browser in it.
  • NewFold the title bar away in the installed app: the window’s buttons float over the corner and the app’s top bar becomes the title bar.
  • NewDrag tabs into order. A tab rides with the pointer, the others slide over, and Esc puts it back.
  • PolishThe tab, rearranged: a status dot on the icon’s corner (yellow unsaved, green saved), a click on the icon saves, and the close button sits at the right end.

Run it on your own machine.

Free and open source under the MIT licence. Windows and macOS; your files never leave the computer.
